claims.text: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity.
Irradiation of bulk HfNbTaTiZr will introduce point defects.
The irradiation-induced point defects will scatter acoustic phonons.
Point-defect scattering will reduce the phonon mean free path.
Reducing the phonon mean free path will reduce phonon thermal conductivity.
Acoustic phonons are relevant to lattice thermal conduction.
Irradiated bulk HfNbTaTiZr will have lower phonon thermal conductivity than unchanged, unirradiated bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted reduction applies from nearly 0 to 200 K.
The predicted reduction applies from 300 to 1200 K.
Oxygen impurities may interact with the irradiation-induced defects.
The effect of irradiation-induced defects on electronic thermal conductivity is uncertain.
A 3ω comparison of irradiated and unirradiated specimens over 30–750 K can test the proposed reduction.
Failure of irradiated HfNbTaTiZr to show lower total thermal conductivity than the unirradiated control would falsify the phonon-specific hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction covers nearly 0–200 K and 300–1200 K, but the proposed experiment covers only 30–750 K, leaving the lowest temperatures and 750–1200 K untested.

The prediction is specifically about phonon thermal conductivity, while the experiment measures unspecified total thermal conductivity. Because the electronic contribution is acknowledged as uncertain, an unchanged total conductivity would not decisively show that the phonon contribution failed to decrease.
